extracted.intended_audience: Users and contributors of Macaulay2 (research mathematicians, package authors, and developers)
extracted.subtask_description: A site resource page listing tools, documentation, contribution guidance, installation info, and community links for users and authors of the Macaulay2 software system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred editor: Emacs
rubrics_metrics.description: Emacs is the preferred text editor for use with Macaulay2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Macaulay2 documentation covers Emacs usage; while Emacs is preferred, other editors have support (see vim and Atom entries). No explicit prohibition on other editors is stated, but Emacs is recommended for best integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vim support available
rubrics_metrics.description: A script (vimM2) is provided for running Macaulay2 in vim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you prefer vim, use the provided vimM2 script to integrate Macaulay2 into your workflow. This is presented as an alternative to the preferred Emacs environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atom syntax highlighting available
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a language-macaulay2 package providing Macaulay2 syntax highlighting for Atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install the language-macaulay2 package in Atom to get syntax highlighting support; useful for users who choose Atom over Emacs or vim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package writing should follow the style guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Package authors are directed to documentation and a style guide for writing Macaulay2 packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors extending Macaulay2 should consult the 'package writing' and 'style guide' resources linked from the site to ensure consistent and compatible package structure and coding/style conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow installation and version guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation instructions and version-specific changes are documented (installation on wiki; changes by version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should follow the installation page on the wiki and consult the 'Changes, by version' listing; the page also lists the current stable version (1.25.11 as of Nov 14, 2025) and links to repositories for source and site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and site code are on GitHub
rubrics_metrics.description: The Macaulay2 source code and the website are hosted on GitHub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers and contributors should use the GitHub repositories for accessing source, reporting issues, and contributing code; links are provided on the resources page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug reporting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Users are instructed to file a bug report when encountering issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A link to 'File a bug report' is provided; users should follow that procedure to report bugs to the Macaulay2 project rather than posting informal reports elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides a 'How to cite Macaulay2' link for proper citation of the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers who use Macaulay2 in publications should follow the provided citation instructions to acknowledge the software correctly.
